messages:
Eli Navarro: FYI — Acme Logistics reporting repeated declines during checkout. Customer says card is valid, AVS/CVV mismatch errors from issuer. Example API response we saw in logs below. Can payments team pick this up? :eyes:

Payments Bot: charge.failed - order: ord_9c3, customer: cust_1234, acquirer_code: X31, avs: U, cvv: N, last4: 2345

Eli Navarro: Here is a sanitized snippet from our gateway log (redacted):
```
{
  "status": "declined",
  "decline_code": "card_decline",
  "acquirer_code": "X31",
  "avs_result": "U",
  "cvv_result": "N",
  "billing_address": {
    "line1": "PO Box 1234",
    "city": "Portsmouth",
    "postal_code": "PO1 3AB",
    "country": "GB"
  }
}
```

Maya Patel: Thanks Eli. Two quick Qs — is the customer using a company card that has a PO BOX in the billing address? And is the merchant configured to allow PO BOX cards? Some acquirers reject PO BOX AVS by contract.

Eli Navarro: Yes, they said their corporate cards list PO Box. Merchant (mid: 555666) is a small B2B seller; I don't see a POBOX allowance flag on their onboarding.

Samir Khan: I'll reproduce. Quick note — our address normalizer currently replaces 'P.O. Box' -> 'PO BOX' and strips punctuation. That can change AVS canonicalization.

Jess Ortega: Also double-check whether we send country-specific postal formatting. UK AVS match tends to require exact postal_code format. If we normalize too aggressively the acquirer will see mismatch.

Samir Khan: Repro steps I used locally:
1) curl our /charges endpoint with original customer payload (billing address exactly as provided)
2) compare with payload after normalizer

Curl example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/charges \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \n  -d '{"amount":1000,"currency":"GBP","card":{"number":"****2345","exp_month":12,"exp_year":2028},"billing_address":{"line1":"PO Box 1234","city":"Portsmouth","postal_code":"PO1 3AB","country":"GB"}}'
```

Samir Khan: Results — original payload -> acquirer returns acquirer_code=X31/avs=U/cvv=N (decline). If I set preserve_billing_address=true in our request pipeline (bypassing normalization) the same card succeeded once. So normalization looks suspect.

Maya Patel: That's useful. Two threads of action: (A) short-term: allow merchant to opt into preserve_billing_address for this MID and test a small batch (we can gate by risk rules). (B) long-term: audit normalizer rules for PO BOX and country-specific treatments.

Eli Navarro: Customer confirmed one success after we toggled the preserve flag, but several other cards still fail — some issuers categorically reject PO Boxes (per acquirer T&Cs). We should escalate to acquirer ops to confirm if MID 555666 is allowed to accept PO BOX billing.

Payments Bot: ticket.created - payments/ops - #PAY-876: Escalate MID 555666 to acquirer ops (include sample payloads and headers)

Jess Ortega: When escalating, include: the raw request/response, merchant contract (showing PO BOX clause), and a note about normalization test that toggled preserve_billing_address=true (include timestamps). Also ask acquirer what their AVS mapping for X31 is — we currently map X31 -> AVS_MISMATCH.

Samir Khan: Quick ask for SRE/infra: can we pull the last 24h of normalization transforms for mid 555666? I want to check whether other merchants saw the same failure pattern. @eng-sre please advise.

Maya Patel: Next actions assigned:
- Samir: run bulk run of preserved vs normalized A/B for last 50 failed charges (due EOD)
- Maya: open acquirer ops escalation, include contract and sample payloads
- Eli: coordinate with customer success to ask Acme Logistics for alternate card or ACH as fallback
- Jess: add test vectors to our AVS regression suite to catch PO BOX regressions

Eli Navarro: Customer success note: Acme is sensitive — they have invoices tied to PO numbers. If we force them to change billing to non-POBOX it will be a blocker. Priority: medium-high.

Samir Khan: I'll drop logs here when complete. For immediate mitigation I'm going to enable preserve_billing_address for that MID and add a temporary rule to skip PO BOX normalization for GB cards.

Jess Ortega: Sounds good. Please document the change in the rollout channel and flag for follow-up to remove the skip after we have acquirer confirmation. :white_check_mark:

Eli Navarro: Thanks team. I'll update the customer once we have acquirer response.

charge-monitor: monitored.event - 3 more fails for ord_9c3 variants in last 10m, queuing for payments ops
